slides.title: India's Literacy Journey
slides.subtitle: Progress, disparities and priorities | Evidence briefing

slides.title: The headline: strong progress, unfinished inclusion
bullets: India's literacy rate rose from 64.84% in 2001 to 74.04% in Census 2011.
The 2011 gender gap was 16.68 percentage points: male 82.14% versus female 65.46%.
The rural–urban gap was 15.20 points: rural 68.91% versus urban 84.11%.
The next challenge is not only access to school, but foundational learning and equitable attainment.
The latest all-India population-census benchmark remains 2011; newer survey estimates should not be mixed without noting methodology.

slides.title: Place matters: rural and urban literacy
State variation is wide
source_ids: Census of India 2011, Primary Census Abstract

slides.title: What the evidence points toward
bullets: Target girls and women in rural and underserved communities with flexible, locally delivered literacy programmes.
Pair enrolment and attendance measures with foundational reading and numeracy assessments.
Use state-level diagnostics rather than a single national average to allocate resources.
Track outcomes by gender, residence, age, disability and socioeconomic status.
Refresh the baseline with the newest official release before making current-year claims; this deck uses the comparable 2011 census benchmark.

slides.title: How to read the numbers
slides.quote: A person aged seven years and above who can both read and write with understanding in any language is treated as literate.
slides.source: Census of India 2011: Census Handbook / Primary Census Abstract
